replies.text:
Check of commonly-missed items:

1. Automated abuse reachable by anyone — design says "An assistant reads each employee's inbox and calendar. When an email asks for a meeting, it books a slot" → covered by listed threat 7 (email flood → calendar spam + LLM cost).
2. Staff/admin/moderator screens showing other people's content — design describes no admin, moderation or support screen. Not present.
3. Delete/moderate/refund/role-change without a record — design says "It acts without asking the employee first"; accountability already covered by listed threat 6.
4. Personal/financial pages browsers, proxies or CDNs could cache — no page, download or HTTP response described. Not present.
5. Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, exports, emails or another interpreting system — the agent "sends invites to the people named in the email", so outsider-chosen recipients/text reach a third system; the recipient-list side (confirming internal addresses, availability, meeting context to an outsider) is **not covered** — listed threat 4 covers spoofed/lookalike attendees and invites appearing to come from the employee, not disclosure to the outsider of internal identities and free/busy. Reporting this one.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["email-triggered assistant", "LLM reasoning step", "calendar booking action", "invite sender", "drive attachment lookup"],
    "dataStores": ["employee mailbox", "employee calendar", "employee drive"],
    "externalServices": ["email", "calendar", "LLM provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["inbound email from outside the company", "employee data accessed by the agent"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": true
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Outsider names internal people in a meeting request and harvests valid addresses, availability and meeting context",
      "scenario": "An outsider emails an employee a meeting request naming a list of guessed or known internal people. The agent books a slot and invites exactly those people, so the outsider receives an invite thread confirming which internal addresses are real, who was free at that time, and the meeting context the agent drew from the inbox. Repeating with different name lists and times maps staff and free/busy schedules across the company, with no employee in the loop because the agent 'acts without asking'.",
      "component": "invite sender / attendee list taken from email body",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "personal_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "it books a slot, sends invites to the people named in the email" },
        { "quote": "It acts without asking the employee first." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V8.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-204"],
      "plainLanguage": "A stranger can email a meeting request listing guessed internal names, and the replies tell them which staff exist and when they are free.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Do not disclose internal attendees or availability to external requesters",
        "given": "a meeting request arrives from an address outside the organisation naming internal attendees",
        "when": "the assistant prepares to book and invite",
        "then": "it must not invite or expose internal attendee addresses, free/busy results or inbox-derived meeting context to the external sender without the employee's explicit approval"
      }
    }
  ]
}
